step1_identity.benchmark_type_evidence: SEA-HELM is a curated suite of SEA datasets which are evaluated together... SEA-HELM (a) incorporates natively adapted and human-translated benchmark tasks from a range of SEA languages... (b) created the human-translated SEA-IFEval and SEA-MTBench datasets; and (c) constructed LLM prompt templates in each native language... SEA-HELM includes new datasets we developed for granular linguistic diagnostics (LINDSEA)
step1_identity.brief_description: SEA-HELM (SouthEast Asian Holistic Evaluation of Language Models) is a holistic multilingual and multicultural LLM evaluation suite for Southeast Asian languages, comprising five core pillars: NLP Classics, LLM-Specifics, SEA Linguistics, SEA Culture, and Safety. It currently supports Filipino, Indonesian, Tamil, Thai, and Vietnamese, combining collated native-language and translated datasets with newly created benchmarks (SEA-IFEval, SEA-MTBench, LINDSEA).

datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: Table 1 marks these datasets as Native=Y with no translation source. Paper states: 'We selected datasets that comprised of data originally written in the native language as far as possible.'

details.KALAHI: Explicitly participatory approach with native Filipino community; designed to test culturally-specific situations Filipinos encounter in daily lives
details.LINDSEA: Handcrafted linguistic diagnostics for Indonesian and Tamil, grounded in extensive literature on these languages' specific phenomena
details.SEA-IFEval: Translated from English but culturally localised to remove biases and ensure cultural authenticity
details.SEA-MTBench: Translated from English but manually localised for SEA cultural context
details.native_datasets: Remaining native datasets reflect local contexts (social media, news, elections, etc.)

all_annotators_native_speakers.value: partially: for SEA-HELM's own datasets (SEA-IFEval, SEA-MTBench, LINDSEA), native speakers were involved; for collated external datasets, annotator info is not provided in this paper
all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: consisting of paid native speakers of SEA languages who worked as translators and annotators... We deliberately incorporate community participation by involving native speakers of the SEA languages at each stage of the dataset planning and construction

affiliations: Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM), Stanford University
annotator_workforce.compensation_details: compensation and working hours for all members involved were established in full compliance with the prevailing university guidelines and applicable regulations. QA team was recruited through public advertisements that clearly outlined the estimated workload and hourly pay.
annotator_workforce.evidence: The SEA-HELM project has received full and official approval from our university's internal review board after undergoing a rigorous review process. The team is composed predominantly of students at local universities and members of the public. Annotator demographics are not included in this paper for anonymity.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The paper explicitly acknowledges English-centricity as a problem: 'translated datasets often contain elements of translationese which can differ significantly from natively written text.' 11 of 26 datasets are translated from English. The paper prioritises native datasets where possible and localises translated content. IndicXNLI is the only machine-translated dataset. Prompt templates are in native languages rather than English.

also_represented: South Asia (Tamil is also spoken in India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia)
geographic_representation.evidence: SEA-HELM currently supports Filipino, Indonesian, Tamil, Thai, and Vietnamese. Paper acknowledges plans to expand to Khmer, Lao, Burmese, etc. The SEA region is home to nearly 700 million speakers across more than 1,000 languages. Currently covers 5 of 11 SEA countries.
